prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single B007 part naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The chair asks us to fix the principle before choosing the third name, so I state mine. The prize rewards a discovery that changes the field, and the citation should name what was found. Here that is the proglucagon-derived hormone, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide, its receptor biology, and the identity and synthesis of the active peptide. Those findings explain the incretin effect, and every later step, including the long-acting agonists and the outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease, rests on them. Holst, Drucker and Mojsov map onto that chain. The therapeutic consequence belongs in the citation as the result of the discovery, as in my wording, and does not need a named developer. The achievement is mature, with decades of independent confirmation, so there is no timing argument for waiting.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still the third name. Mojsov's priority for the active form is disputed in the literature, Habener is not on the supplied list, and I cannot verify the priority question from the record in front of us. Naming her could therefore be read as a ruling on a contested history, and leaving out Knudsen means the person most identified with turning the peptide into a usable drug goes unnamed. I accept that a discovery-first prize can look like it skips the step that delivered the benefit. The citation must therefore be worded narrowly: it should claim only physiology and identification of the active form, which the credited names support, and must not claim first discovery of the active peptide against others outside the list.

responses.point: Sandberg and the chair argue that acylation-based half-life extension is what made the physiology a medicine, so Knudsen should take the third place under a citation naming both physiology and long-acting agonists. Sandberg also says he would accept the Mojsov trio if the committee wants a purely discovery-level prize.
responses.response: The principle is the real disagreement, so I will answer it directly. I do not dispute that the acylation design was original and decisive for the outcome trials. My difficulty is that a citation naming the development of long-acting agonists turns the prize into one for a product line, and the Medicine prize has been most defensible when it names what was found. I also do not accept that a contested priority is a reason to prefer Knudsen. Priority uncertainty is a reason to word the citation carefully, not to remove the person tied to the active peptide. Your conditional offer matters, because it means the gap between us is about principle and not about merit. I ask that the committee adopt the discovery-level principle explicitly and let the therapeutic consequence appear only as the result of the discovery. I have not changed my view, and nothing in your round-1 text shows that Mojsov's contribution is subordinate to Knudsen's.

responses.point: The chair finds Knudsen's contribution documented in approved drugs, while Mojsov's credit cannot be verified from the supplied text and is entangled with early contributors. He says he would move if the committee judges peptide identification more decisive.
responses.response: I agree that the Mojsov credit cannot be verified from the supplied text, and I will not claim it is settled. But an unverified claim cuts both ways. If we exclude her because it is unverified, the committee settles the priority question against her without evidence, and that is a decision too. The supplied credit names her for identification and synthesis of the active form, and I take the list as the evidence I have. On your point that the prize has recognised the step that makes a discovery usable, I accept it for some past prizes, but in those cases the usable step was usually part of the discovery arc and not a separate industrial engineering programme. I would give your argument more weight if the record showed that the long-acting analogues changed our understanding of the physiology, and from what I have it showed that they changed delivery. Please test whether the discovery-first principle would still convince you if the third name were the only open point.

responses.point: Linnarsson backs the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio on a discovery-centred citation, would move only if the record showed Mojsov's priority to be weaker than credited, and ranks B004 below B041 as the first alternative because of its translational immaturity.
responses.response: We are aligned on the trio and I accept your warning that a result this far ahead of the field risks an untested allocation, which is why I have tried to state the principle plainly this round. On the alternatives, I keep B004 first because the decision is only needed if B007 stalls on credit, and then the question is which alternative has the credit that can be defended. Walter and Mori are a coherent pair with a secure mechanism, while B041 still has the Eshhar originator problem outside the credited names, which you also raised. I accept your point that B041 has the stronger clinical record. I do not think that settles the order when the cause of the stall is attribution. I have not changed the order of B004 and B041.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would keep the three people whose work established what the active peptide is and does, notes that Habener is not on the list, and says leaving out Mojsov settles the uncertainty against her without evidence.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning and with the wording that anchors the citation in physiology and the active form. I would add one practical condition on the citation. Because Habener is outside the supplied credit, the text should not say that the credited names were the first to identify the active peptide, only that they made discoveries of the physiology and identification of the active form. Your remark that B004's clean attribution depends on the supplied list is also fair, because Ron and Kaufman are not credited there. That is why I describe B004 as the cleaner alternative among the listed names and not as a settled prize, and why I do not claim more for it than the record supports.

responses.point: El Manira holds Drucker and Holst fixed, leans toward Mojsov on a discovery-first reading, and calls the third name a judgement call that he wants tested again in round 2.
responses.response: I have tried to test it. The strongest case against Mojsov is not on science but on proof, since her priority is disputed and I cannot resolve it from the record. The strongest case for her is that the committee would be choosing between an uncertain credit on the discovery side and an undisputed development contribution, and that choice depends entirely on the principle. Once the committee agrees the prize is for a discovery, the choice follows. I also agree with you that a B004 pairing with B007 does not fit, since Drucker and Holst alone would weaken the main part, so I treat this as a single-part prize.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 form is sufficiently established against Habener and others outside the supplied list. I cannot resolve this from the supplied record and have no basis to claim confidential information.

Whether the committee will adopt a discovery-level principle for B007 or a discovery-plus-development principle. My configuration depends on this and I would reconsider only if the record showed the long-acting analogue work changed understanding of the physiology.
If B007 stalls, whether B004 or B041 resolves its credit problem more easily: Ron and Kaufman outside the B004 credit, or Eshhar and the Rosenberg question for B041.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any B007, B004 or B041 candidate. I co-authored nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans at Salk, and he is not credited on any shortlisted ballot. I have co-authored works with Per Svenningsson, who chairs the committee, and one work with Abdel El Manira. None concerns a shortlisted achievement, and I see no need for recusal. My disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
